title: Make Duplicate Delivery Safe
description: A queue consumer updates a wallet and records the processed event ID in the same relational database. Which approach prevents a redelivered event from applying the balance change twice?

options.text: Acknowledge the message before updating the database.
options.explanation: A crash after acknowledgement but before the update can lose the effect entirely.

options.text: Read the processed-event table, then update the balance and insert the event ID in separate commits.
options.explanation: Concurrent consumers can both pass the read check, and a crash between commits can leave the balance and deduplication state inconsistent.

options.text: Use a unique scoped event ID and commit the deduplication record with the balance change in one transaction, then acknowledge.
options.explanation: The unique constraint handles concurrent duplicates and the transaction binds the business effect to its deduplication record. A crash before acknowledgement can then be safely retried.

options.text: Generate a new random event ID on every retry.
options.explanation: Changing the ID makes the same logical operation look new and defeats deduplication.
